harness.name: Bank Harness — Requirements Assistant
harness.purpose: Refine requirements for the bank-harness solution, and operate the solution as a whole.
owns: anything that spans more than one repository
running the solution end to end
harness.pathNote: All paths are RELATIVE by design. Absolute paths broke once already when these repos were moved into muli-repo/ — do not reintroduce them.

knowledgeBases.summary: The canonical business knowledge for the banking product: vocabulary, domain concepts, rules, journeys, constraints. Written to be read without any codebase.

conventions.[intent]: stakeholder-confirmed direction, NOT built — never cite as an active rule
conventions.[gap]: known limitation with a business consequence

repositories.summary: Banking service. Holds every account and transaction, and enforces every rule about money.

understand.graphShape: version, project, nodes, edges, layers, tour
understand.freshnessCheck: compare .ua/meta.json gitCommitHash against the repo's current HEAD; if they differ the graph predates the working tree

repositories.doNotEditReason: Generated and maintained by tooling (/codebase-discovery and /understand). Hand edits are clobbered on the next run and diverge from what the tooling believes it wrote.

repositories.summary: Customer-facing application. Presents accounts and history, collects input, decides nothing about money.

understand.graphShape: version, project, nodes, edges, layers, tour
understand.freshnessCheck: compare .ua/meta.json gitCommitHash against the repo's current HEAD; if they differ the graph predates the working tree

repositories.doNotEditReason: Generated and maintained by tooling (/codebase-discovery and /understand). Hand edits are clobbered on the next run and diverge from what the tooling believes it wrote.

refinement.versioning: One version per completed refinement pass. Re-refining increments n; earlier versions are never edited or deleted.
refinement.questionIds: Q<n>, allocated globally in order across the whole session and never reused, including across versions.
refinement.portability: state.md carries everything needed to resume on another machine or tool. No state is held outside the requirement folder.

contextLoading._comment: Read at the start of EVERY session, before any other work. This is the resolved form of the `entry` field on each knowledgeBase and repository — if an entry is added or renamed there, update this list too.

atSessionStart.why: How this harness works and the rules of engagement. Loads automatically as project context.
Canonical business knowledge — vocabulary, rules, journeys, constraints. Read before the repos.
What the banking service is and how it is organised, plus its own caveats.
What the customer application is and how it is organised, plus its own caveats.

contextLoading.rationale: Each repo's CLAUDE.md is its own maintained orientation. Loading all of them means the harness starts with the whole solution in view rather than discovering it mid-task, and it inherits each repo's stated caveats — including which files must never be hand-edited.
contextLoading.thenOnDemand: Deeper documents are pulled per question via the `routing` section below. Do not bulk-load docs/ or .ua/ at session start.

commands.purpose: Entry point for refinement. Resolves the target folder, decides new / resume / re-refine, then hands off to the skill.

skills.purpose: Run a resumable requirement-refinement session: load context, interview, record every question and answer, produce an agreed requirement.
skills.useWhen: Refining a requirement.md into requirements-v<n>.md, resuming a paused session, or re-refining an existing one.

skills.purpose: Interview the requester one question at a time to turn a vague ask into a confirmed requirement, checked against the knowledge base.
skills.useWhen: A request is underspecified, or before writing anything into requirements/.
skills.produces: A confirmed intent statement that maps onto templates/requirement.md

routing._comment: Which source answers which kind of question. Consult in this order; stop at the first that answers.

runtime._comment: Verified 2026-07-22. Start in this order — the service exits immediately if its datastore is unreachable at startup.

components.notes: Also starts an admin UI on 8081. Data persists across restarts.
Exposes interactive API documentation, usable on its own without the customer application.
Proxies API calls to the service, so the browser stays same-origin.

knownIssues: No seed data exists anywhere. A fresh datastore has no accounts; create one and deposit before withdrawal or transfer will work.
The customer application defines a lint script whose tool is not installed — it fails.

workingAgreements: Read the knowledge base before the code. It is the canonical source for business language and rules.
Never edit anything under doNotEdit. Those docs are tool-generated.
Requirements are written in business language. If a requirement can only be understood with a file open, it is a task, not a requirement.
Do not invent rules. If the knowledge base does not state it, it is not a rule — check constraints and decisions before assuming.
[intent] items are not built. Never write a requirement that assumes one is already in place.
When refinement establishes a new business fact, update the knowledge base — not the repositories.
